mapper.select:
-- ====================================================== -- STEP 1: CALCULATE POSTED JOURNAL ACTIVITY -- ======================================================
/* Aggregate posted ledger entries by account.
We calculate a debit/credit difference using exact PostgreSQL NUMERIC arithmetic.
Here we initially use:
credits - debits
This is positive for normal revenue activity.
Expenses will have their sign reversed in the final SELECT statement.
COUNT(*) records how many posted ledger entries contributed to each account.
This is important because a zero net amount does not necessarily mean there was no financial activity. */
WITH posted_activity AS (
SELECT le.business_id, le.account_id,
-- ============================================== -- CREDIT-POSITIVE NET FINANCIAL ACTIVITY -- ==============================================
SUM( le.credit - le.debit ) AS net_credit_activity,
-- ============================================== -- NUMBER OF POSTED LEDGER ENTRIES -- ==============================================
COUNT(*) AS posted_entry_count
FROM ledger_entries le
-- ============================================== -- JOIN LEDGER ENTRIES TO THEIR TRANSACTIONS -- ==============================================
/* Join using both business_id and transaction_id for business isolation. */
INNER JOIN transactions t ON t.business_id = le.business_id AND t.id = le.transaction_id
WHERE le.business_id = #{businessId}
-- ============================================ -- INCLUDE POSTED TRANSACTIONS ONLY -- ============================================
AND t.status = 'POSTED'
-- ============================================ -- INCLUSIVE REPORTING START DATE -- ============================================
AND t.transaction_date >= #{startDate}
-- ============================================ -- INCLUSIVE REPORTING END DATE -- ============================================
AND t.transaction_date <= #{endDate}
-- ============================================== -- AGGREGATE ACTIVITY PER ACCOUNT -- ==============================================
GROUP BY le.business_id, le.account_id )
-- ====================================================== -- STEP 2: SELECT REVENUE AND EXPENSE ACCOUNTS -- ======================================================
SELECT
-- ============================================== -- ACCOUNT IDENTIFICATION -- ==============================================
a.id AS account_id, a.code, a.name,
-- ============================================== -- ACCOUNT CLASSIFICATION -- ==============================================
a.account_type, a.reporting_group,
-- ============================================== -- ACCOUNT STATUS -- ==============================================
a.is_active,
-- ================================================== -- STEP 3: APPLY CORRECT ACCOUNTING SIGNS -- ==================================================
/* Revenue accounts have a normal CREDIT balance.
Revenue amount:
credits - debits
Expense accounts have a normal DEBIT balance.
Expense amount:
debits - credits
Because posted_activity stores credits - debits, we negate that amount for expenses.
Preserve negative results rather than automatically forcing amounts to zero. */
CASE
-- ========================================== -- REVENUE: CREDITS MINUS DEBITS -- ==========================================
WHEN a.account_type = 'REVENUE' THEN
COALESCE( pa.net_credit_activity, 0::NUMERIC )
-- ========================================== -- EXPENSE: DEBITS MINUS CREDITS -- ==========================================
WHEN a.account_type = 'EXPENSE' THEN
-COALESCE( pa.net_credit_activity, 0::NUMERIC )
-- ========================================== -- DEFENSIVE DEFAULT -- ==========================================
ELSE 0::NUMERIC
END AS amount,
-- ================================================== -- STEP 4: RETURN POSTED ENTRY COUNT -- ==================================================
/* If the account has no posted entries during the period, return zero.
This count allows the Java service to distinguish:
- An unused account with zero activity - An account with offsetting activity whose net amount is zero */
COALESCE( pa.posted_entry_count, 0::BIGINT ) AS posted_entry_count
-- ====================================================== -- STEP 5: INCLUDE ALL RELEVANT BUSINESS ACCOUNTS -- ======================================================
FROM accounts a
/* LEFT JOIN ensures that revenue and expense accounts without posted activity still appear with amount = 0.
Inactive accounts are not filtered out.
Unclassified accounts are not filtered out. */
LEFT JOIN posted_activity pa ON pa.business_id = a.business_id AND pa.account_id = a.id
-- ====================================================== -- STEP 6: APPLY BUSINESS AND ACCOUNT FILTERS -- ======================================================
WHERE a.business_id = #{businessId}
-- ================================================ -- ONLY INCOME STATEMENT ACCOUNT TYPES -- ================================================
AND a.account_type IN ( 'REVENUE', 'EXPENSE' )
-- ================================================ -- ONLY DIRECT POSTING ACCOUNTS -- ================================================
/* Grouping accounts organize the Chart of Accounts but cannot directly receive journal entries.
We do not sum child balances into a parent account in this query.
This prevents double-counting.
Reporting-group subtotals will be calculated separately in Java. */
AND a.is_postable = TRUE
-- ====================================================== -- STEP 7: SORT FINANCIAL ACCOUNTS -- ======================================================
/* Display Revenue accounts before Expenses.
Then order accounts by customizable account codes and database IDs.
The final financial statement service will organize these accounts further into reporting-group sections. */
ORDER BY
CASE WHEN a.account_type = 'REVENUE' THEN 1 WHEN a.account_type = 'EXPENSE' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END,
a.code, a.id
